should: I want to see how the config on our live server differs from my repo without importing anything. How do I do that with drush?
How do I set up a local config split so devel and kint are only enabled on my machine?
After I pulled the prod database and ran drush cex, git shows my new field config as deleted. What happened?
What is the difference between a complete split and a partial split in Drupal config_split?
should_not: Update the drupal/webform module with Composer and apply a patch from the issue queue.

cases.prompt: I want to preview the config differences on our remote server over SSH before I import. Give me the exact command.
expected: uses drush cim with --no and --diff (or config:import --no --diff)
explains that remote drush may default to --yes and auto-import without the --no flag
offers read-only alternatives such as config:get or config:status
must_not: gives a remote drush cim --diff command without --no
suggests running a remote drush cim to see what would change
grounded_in: **CRITICAL**: Always use `--no` flag with remote drush! Without it, commands may auto-confirm.
Use `config:get` and `config:status` for read-only inspection, or use `--no` flag with `cim`/`cex` to prevent auto-confirmation.

cases.prompt: I have uncommitted work on a new field and I need to bring production config into my local repo. What order should I do things in?
expected: says to commit local changes first
then pull the production database (for example ddev pull --environment=live) and run drush config:export
then review the git diff on the config directory before committing the prod changes
must_not: suggests exporting config before committing local feature work
grounded_in: **Step 1: Commit local changes first**
**Purpose**: Safely merge production config changes while preserving local feature work.

cases.prompt: After exporting config from the prod database, git status shows my new field.storage and field.field files as deleted, plus some modified UUIDs and a changed views file. What do I keep and what do I revert?
expected: says the deleted files are the new local feature and should be restored with git checkout HEAD -- <file>
says UUID-only modifications from prod should be kept
says changed prod config such as views should be kept after review
must_not: tells the user to commit the deletions
grounded_in: git checkout HEAD -- config/default/field.storage.node.your_new_field.yml
Your new feature files deleted by prod export

cases.prompt: I want a different Search API server connector (local Solr) in my local environment while production keeps its own. Should this be a complete or partial config split?
expected: recommends a partial split because the config exists everywhere with different values
explains a partial split keeps base config in config/default and stores overrides in the split directory
contrasts it with a complete split, which removes config entirely when the split is inactive
must_not: recommends a complete split for a config object that must also exist in production
grounded_in: Config exists everywhere but with different VALUES
**Complete split** = Config is REMOVED from `config/default/` and moved to split directory entirely

cases.prompt: Every time I run drush cex, config/default/search_api.server.main.yml disappears. Why, and how do I fix it?
expected: identifies the most likely cause as the config being in complete_list instead of partial_list
says to move the config from complete_list to partial_list in the split definition and re-export
says to check that config/default still has the file and config/local has the config_split.patch file
grounded_in: **Root cause (99% of cases)**: Config is in `complete_list` instead of `partial_list`!
**Solution**: Move from `complete_list` to `partial_list`

cases.prompt: I edited config/default/config_split.config_split.local.yml to add a partial_list entry but nothing changed on export. Why?
expected: explains that split definition changes must be in active configuration (the database), not just the exported files
suggests importing the change (for example config:import --partial) or setting it via drush php:eval, then exporting
grounded_in: **⚠️ IMPORTANT**: When updating config split definitions, changes must be in **ACTIVE configuration** (database), not just exported files!
**Import to make active**: `ddev drush config:import --partial` OR use PHP (see below)

cases.prompt: I only want to bring one config object, views.view.content, from my YAML files into the active config on my local DDEV site. How?
expected: suggests config:import --partial with --source=config/default, or config:set for specific values
does not run a full unreviewed config import of everything
grounded_in: ddev drush config:import --partial --source=config/default
ddev drush config:set config.name key.subkey value

cases.prompt: drush cim fails because of a UUID mismatch and system.site is complaining. What are my options?
expected: suggests the --partial flag for the UUID mismatch
notes some config such as system.site has immutable values or is locked
mentions --skip-config=system.site to skip specific config during import
grounded_in: **UUID mismatch**: Use `--partial` flag
ddev drush config:import --skip-config=system.site

cases.prompt: My local config split does not seem to activate. How do I check and fix it?
expected: checks the split status with config-split:status
activates it with config-split:activate and the split name
runs drush cex afterwards to save the activation state
grounded_in: ddev drush cex  # Export to save activation state
ddev drush config-split:activate {split-name}

cases.prompt: I synced a few config values from dev by hand. How should I commit them?
expected: recommends editing the config files directly and reviewing git diff
recommends one config type per commit with a message naming the source environment
grounded_in: **One config type per commit** - Separate concerns for clean history
**Preferred**: Edit config files directly, then commit:
